blocks.task_summary: Show that w = sqrt(3) + i by rationalizing the denominator.
method_path: Multiply numerator and denominator by conjugate of denominator

evidence.basis: attempt to multiply by conjugate M1; 4i/(1+i sqrt(3)) * (1-i sqrt(3))/(1-i sqrt(3)) = (4 sqrt(3) + 4i)/4, (i(1-i sqrt(3))) A1; w = sqrt(3) + i AG
(b)(i) attempt to find either |w| or arg w (M1); |w| = sqrt(3+1) OR arctan(1/sqrt(3)) OR labelled diagram; |w| = 2 A1; (ii) arg w = pi/6 A1

blocks.task_summary: Use De Moivre's theorem to find the two square roots of w in the form re^(iθ).
method_path: Apply De Moivre's theorem with n=1/2 to get first root: sqrt(2)e^(iπ/12)
Add π to argument to get second root: sqrt(2)e^(i(π/12+π)) = sqrt(2)e^(i13π/12) = sqrt(2)e^(-i11π/12)

evidence.basis: attempt to find a root using de Moivre's theorem with n=1/2 (M1); sqrt(2)e^(iπ/12) A1; attempt to find second root by adding or subtracting π from their argument (M1); sqrt(2)e^(-11πi/12) A1

blocks.task_summary: Given w = (a+bi)^2 with a,b>0, show a^2 = (sqrt(3)+1)/2 and find b^2.
method_path: Equate to sqrt(3) + i: a^2 - b^2 = sqrt(3), 2ab = 1
Solve quadratic in a^2: a^2 = (4sqrt(3) ± sqrt(48+16))/8 = (sqrt(3) ± 1)/2
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: Use polar form w = 2e^(iπ/6), then a+bi = sqrt(2)e^(iπ/12), equate real part a = sqrt(2)cos(π/12), square and use double angle to get a^2 = (sqrt(3)+1)/2.

evidence.basis: (d)(i) METHOD 1: attempt to expand and equate to sqrt(3)+i (M1); a^2 - b^2 + 2abi = sqrt(3) + i; at least one correct equation A1; a^2 - b^2 = sqrt(3) OR 2ab = 1; substituting b = 1/(2a) (M1); a^2 - (1/(2a))^2 = sqrt(3); 4a^4 - 4sqrt(3)a^2 - 1 = 0 A1; attempt to solve quadratic in a^2 M1; a^2 = (4sqrt(3) ± sqrt(48+16))/8 = (sqrt(3) ± 1)/2; since a^2 > 0 R1; a^2 = (sqrt(3)+1)/2 AG; METHOD 2: w = a+bi (A1); a+bi = sqrt(2)(cos(π/12) + i sin(π/12)) A1; attempt to equate Re(w) M1; a = sqrt(2)cos(π/12); a^2 = 2cos^2(π/12) A1; attempt to use double angle formula (M1); cos2α = 2cos^2α - 1; a^2 = 2cos^2(π/12) = cos(π/6)+1 = sqrt(3)/2 + 1 A1; a^2 = (sqrt(3)+1)/2 AG; (ii) attempt to substitute a^2 into a^2 - b^2 = sqrt(3) OR b^2 = 1/(4a^2) (M1); b^2 = (sqrt(3)+1)/2 - sqrt(3) = (sqrt(3)-1)/2 A1

method_path: Recognize that tan(π/12) = b/a from the complex number a+bi = sqrt(2)e^(iπ/12)

evidence.basis: attempt to set up an equation using an argument of π/12 (M1); tan(π/12) = b/a (A1); substitution of the given a and their b M1; sqrt((sqrt(3)-1)/2) / sqrt((sqrt(3)+1)/2) = sqrt((sqrt(3)-1)/(sqrt(3)+1)) A1; tan(π/12) = 2 - sqrt(3), accept p=2, q=-1 A1
